translations.comment: Button an agent clicks to open a closed support ticket back up

alternativesConsidered.rejectedBecause: Correct verb, but the comment says the ticket was closed and is being opened back up, which Spanish marks with the re- prefix.
An adjective describing a state. This is a button, so it needs a command.

translations.disambiguationNote: This is a button an agent presses, so Spanish needs a verb, not a description. The comment says the ticket is being opened back up after being closed, so "Reabrir" (reopen) is more precise than plain "Abrir".

translations.comment: Label shown when the support desk is currently open for business

alternativesConsidered.rejectedBecause: That is a command. Nothing is being clicked here — the label describes the desk's current state.

translations.disambiguationNote: Same English word as the ticket button, opposite grammar. This one reports that the support desk is currently open for business, so Spanish uses the adjective "Abierto".

translations.comment: Button an agent clicks to mark a ticket as resolved/closed

alternativesConsidered.rejectedBecause: A state, not an action. Wrong form for a button.
Reads well, but the source says Close and the paired reopen button is "Reabrir"; keeping the open/close pairing is clearer.

translations.disambiguationNote: A button, so the infinitive "Cerrar". It pairs with "Reabrir" on the same ticket.

translations.comment: Button to publish a new post to the internal team feed

alternativesConsidered.rejectedBecause: That is the postal sense of "post". This button publishes to a feed.
Means send. Publishing to a shared feed is more specific.

translations.disambiguationNote: "Post" here is the verb used in social feeds, not anything to do with mail. As a button it takes the infinitive "Publicar".

translations.comment: Label for a physical mail correspondence address field

alternativesConsidered.rejectedBecause: The feed sense of "post". This field is about physical mail.
Ambiguous in Spanish — it reads as email first. "Postal" removes the doubt.

translations.disambiguationNote: Same English word as the feed button, completely different meaning. This is a field label for a physical correspondence address, so it needs a noun phrase, and "postal" is what stops Spanish readers assuming email.
assumptions: Read as the label for the address field itself rather than a section heading above several fields.

translations.comment: Button to assign a ticket to a specific agent
translations.disambiguationNote: Unambiguous. A button, so the infinitive.

translations.comment: Field showing the due date/deadline for resolving a ticket

alternativesConsidered.rejectedBecause: Accurate but long for a field label; "Vencimiento" already reads as the due date in Spanish UIs.
Means overdue. The field shows the deadline, not whether it has passed.

translations.disambiguationNote: The deadline for resolving a ticket. A field label, so a noun.

translations.comment: Field showing the amount of money owed on an invoice

alternativesConsidered.rejectedBecause: That is the due date sense. This field is money owed, not a date.
Means overdue — it asserts the payment is late, which the English does not.

translations.disambiguationNote: Same English word as the ticket deadline field, but the key and comment both say this is an amount of money. "Importe adeudado" is the balance owed and says nothing about whether it is late.

translations.disambiguationNote: Unambiguous. A button, so the infinitive.

The English "Open" here is the action of reopening a closed ticket, and this translation picked the meaning "is currently open" instead.
